title: Weather, nature & seasons
goal: Talk about the weather and seasons, describe Sindh's landscapes, and say what the weather is going to do.
intro:
Sindh is one of the hottest places on earth: long, blazing summers, a short monsoon that can bring floods, and a mild, lovely winter. Weather talk is therefore mostly about **گرمي** (garmī, heat) — and the relief of rain (**مينهن**, mīṃhu).

Grammatically, weather is expressed with **nouns** rather than 'it is …': 'heat is' (گرمي آهي), 'rain is falling' (مينهن پيو وسي). You'll also take a first look at the **future** for forecasts: مينهن **وسندو** 'it will rain'.

vocab.note: f. ڏاڍي گرمي آهي = it's very hot.
f. مون کي ٿڌ لڳي ٿي = I feel cold.
m. واءُ لڳي ٿو = the wind is blowing.
f. مٽي جو طوفان = dust storm.
m. ڪارونجهر جبل = the Karoonjhar hills in Thar.
m. ٿر جو رڻ = the Thar desert.

vocab.en: to seem, feel; to strike, be attached
vocab.note: لڳي ٿو ته … = it seems that …

phrases.native: اڄ ڪڪر آهن، شايد مينهن وسندو.
phrases.roman: aʄu kakara āhin, shāyad mīṃhu vasando.
phrases.en: It's cloudy today; maybe it will rain.

phrases.native: سنڌ ۾ اونهارو ڏاڍو ڊگهو ٿئي ٿو.
phrases.roman: sindha meṃ unhāro ɗāḍho ḍigho thie tho.
phrases.en: Summer in Sindh is very long.

phrases.native: سيارو سڀ کان سٺي موسم آهي.
phrases.roman: siyāro sabha khāṃ suṭhī mausama āhe.

phrases.native: مٽيءَ جو طوفان اچي رهيو آهي.
phrases.roman: miṭīa jo tūfānu achī rahyo āhe.

phrases.native: برسات کان پوءِ ٿر سائو ٿي ٿو وڃي.
phrases.roman: barsāta khāṃ poi thara sāo thī tho vañe.
phrases.en: After the monsoon, Thar turns green.
Tomorrow it will be less hot.

grammar.title: Weather expressions
grammar.body:
Sindhi has no dummy 'it'. Weather is described with a **noun as subject**:

**گرمي آهي** — 'heat is' = it's hot (گرمي f → ڏاڍي گرمي)
**ٿڌ آهي** — it's cold
**مينهن پيو وسي** — 'rain is raining' = it's raining (مينهن m)
**واءُ لڳي ٿو / هوا هلي ٿي** — the wind blows
**ڪڪر آهن** — there are clouds = it's cloudy
**اُس آهي** — there's sunshine

For how **you feel**, use کي + لڳڻ: مون کي ٿڌ لڳي ٿي 'I feel cold', مون کي گرمي لڳي ٿي 'I feel hot'. With پئي for 'right now': مون کي ٿڌ پئي لڳي.

To describe the climate in general, use **ٿئي ٿو / ٿئي ٿي** ('becomes, happens'): سنڌ ۾ گرمي ٿئي ٿي 'in Sindh it gets hot'.

examples.roman: karāchīa meṃ siyāro thoro thie tho.

examples.en: The sun is very strong today.

examples.roman: thara meṃ mīṃhu ghaṭu vase tho.

grammar.title: Forecasts: 'it will' and 'it looks like'
grammar.body:
For predictions you need the **future** (taught fully in Unit 17). For third-person forecasts, add **-ndo** (m) / **-ndī** (f) to the stem:

وسڻ → **وسندو** vasando 'will rain' (مينهن m)
ٿيڻ → **ٿيندي** thīndī 'will become' (گرمي f)
هجڻ 'to be' → **هوندو / هوندي** hundo / hundī 'will be'

To say 'it looks like…', use **لڳي ٿو ته …** 'it seems that …': لڳي ٿو ته مينهن وسندو 'it looks like it's going to rain'. And for 'perhaps' add **شايد**.

examples.en: It looks like a storm is coming.
It'll get cold in the evening.
The weather will be nice next week.

dialogue.title: A trip to Keenjhar Lake?
dialogue.setting: Ayaz and Sarah plan a weekend outing from Karachi.

lines.speaker: Ayaz
lines.en: Shall we go to Keenjhar on Sunday?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.en: Yes! But what will the weather be like?

lines.speaker: Ayaz
lines.native: فون تي ڏسان ٿو… آچر تي ڪڪر هوندا ۽ هلڪو مينهن وسندو.
lines.roman: fon te ɗisāṃ tho… āchara te kakara hundā ai halko mīṃhu vasando.
lines.en: Let me check the phone… On Sunday it'll be cloudy with light rain.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.native: مينهن ۾ ڍنڍ تي وڃڻ ٺيڪ آهي؟
lines.roman: mīṃha meṃ ḍhanḍha te vañaṇu ṭhīku āhe?
lines.en: Is it OK to go to the lake in the rain?

lines.speaker: Ayaz
lines.native: بلڪل! برسات ۾ ڪينجهر ڏاڍي سهڻي لڳي ٿي.
lines.roman: bilkul! barsāta meṃ kīnjhar ɗāḍhī sohaṇī laɠe thī.
lines.en: Absolutely! Keenjhar looks gorgeous in the monsoon.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.en: And it won't be hot, will it?

lines.speaker: Ayaz
lines.native: نه، ڪراچيءَ کان گهٽ. ٿڌي هوا لڳندي.
lines.roman: na, karāchīa khāṃ ghaṭu. thadhī havā laɠandī.
lines.en: No, less than Karachi. There'll be a cool breeze.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.en: Great! Then let's leave early in the morning.

lines.speaker: Ayaz
lines.native: چڱو، ستين وڳي. ڇٽي کڻي اچجو!
lines.roman: chaṅgo, satīṃ vaɠe. chhaṭī khaṇī achijo!
lines.en: OK, seven o'clock. Bring an umbrella!

culture: The **Indus** (سنڌو درياهه) is the lifeline of Sindh — the province takes its name from it, and its canals and barrages irrigate the wheat, rice, cotton and sugarcane fields. **Keenjhar Lake** near Thatta is linked to the legend of Noori and Jam Tamachi, one of the love stories sung by Shah Abdul Latif. The **Thar desert** in the east turns green after the monsoon rains, when peacocks dance and Thari folk music celebrates the season. In 2022 catastrophic monsoon floods (ٻوڏ) submerged large parts of Sindh — a reminder of how much daily life depends on the weather.
